subject.title: Feature request: api.callGatewayMethod() for inter-plugin communication

question: Should OpenClaw expose plugin-to-plugin Gateway method calls to ordinary external plugins, and if so should the API be a typed service/capability contract, an allowlisted request surface, or a broader raw dispatcher?
rationale: The remaining choice changes the public Plugin SDK and Gateway authorization boundary, so automation cannot safely decide the permanent API or trust policy.

options.title: Design a narrow authorized SDK contract
options.body: Expose only approved inter-plugin or host Gateway capabilities with plugin caller attribution, explicit authorization, docs, and contract tests.

options.title: Keep Gateway calls trusted-only
options.body: Treat the current bundled/trusted-official `runtime.gateway.request` surface as the supported boundary and decline ordinary external plugin-to-plugin calls.

options.title: Allow raw method dispatch
options.body: Expose a generic method-string caller to plugins and accept the larger compatibility and security surface as an intentional product decision.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow authorized SDK contract
recommendation.body: Expose only approved inter-plugin or host Gateway capabilities with plugin caller attribution, explicit authorization, docs, and contract tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the current trusted Gateway runtime request subset and has adjacent gateway/plugin bootstrap history, making him the best available routing owner for the boundary choice.
